articles.title: Pantheon Closes $6 Billion Private Equity Secondaries Program Above Target
articles.snippet:
Pantheon has closed its latest global private equity secondaries program with $6 billion in commitments, significantly exceeding the strategy's original $3.5 billion target.
The post Pantheon Closes $6 Billion Private Equity Secondaries Program Above Target appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Pantheon Closes $6 Billion Private Equity Secondaries Program Above Target
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 22, 2026
Pantheon Closes $6 Billion Private Equity Secondaries Program Above Target
Pantheon has closed its latest global private equity secondaries program with $6 billion in commitments, significantly exceeding the strategy’s original $3.5 billion target.
Pantheon Global Secondaries Fund VIII and related vehicles finished fundraising approximately 71% above target, marking the firm’s largest private equity secondaries capital raise to date.
The program attracted continued support from existing investors while also bringing in new limited partners, including significant commitments from investors across Asia and the Middle East.
Pantheon said the fundraising reflects continued institutional demand for private equity secondaries as investors look for diversified exposure, portfolio liquidity, and access to established private equity assets.
The fund will invest across both LP-led and GP-led secondary transactions, with an emphasis on the global mid-market. Pantheon plans to use its existing relationships with private equity managers to target funds and companies it believes can be acquired at attractive valuations.
The strategy is designed to build a diversified portfolio across investment vintages, managers, and geographies, with a particular focus on buyout strategies.
Pantheon said it deployed approximately $3.35 billion across 17 private equity secondary transactions in 2025, highlighting the scale of deal flow available to the strategy.
The firm has been investing in private equity secondaries since 1988, making the strategy a longstanding component of its broader private equity platform. Pantheon’s private equity business represents approximately $41 billion of assets within a broader private markets platform managing roughly $84 billion.
The firm also invests across primary fund commitments and co-investments, in addition to secondaries. Pantheon believes this broader exposure gives it additional data, relationships, and sourcing capabilities when evaluating secondary transactions.
Its global private markets platform spans private equity, infrastructure, and private credit, allowing the firm to evaluate opportunities across multiple asset classes and transaction types.
Pantheon said the latest fundraising underscores investor appetite for experienced secondaries managers capable of sourcing proprietary transactions and selectively accessing hard-to-reach private equity managers.
KEY QUOTES:
“Pantheon is recognized for its early leadership in secondaries, and our private equity secondaries strategy continues to be a compelling way for our investors to access high-quality private equity exposure with the diversification benefits the asset class provides. The depth of our GP relationships and access to extensive data across private equity funds and companies amassed over decades enables us to have conviction and be disciplined about the assets we buy and the partners we back, particularly in the mid-market where access and selection matters most. We enter this next phase with strong conviction in our ability to keep identifying compelling opportunities for our investors.”
Amyn Hassanally, Partner And Global Head Of Private Equity Secondaries At Pantheon

articles.title: Waymo Secures $5 Billion Debt Financing From PIMCO, Blackstone, Sixth Street And Other Lenders
articles.snippet:
Waymo closed a $5 billion term loan, marking the autonomous driving company’s first debt financing as it continues expanding its commercial operations in the United States and internationally. PIMCO, Blackstone, and Sixth Street participated as lead syndicated lenders in the financing. Capital Group, Loomis Sayles, and T. Rowe Price also participated as significant lenders.
The post Waymo Secures $5 Billion Debt Financing From PIMCO, Blackstone, Sixth Street And Other Lenders appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Waymo Secures $5 Billion Debt Financing From PIMCO, Blackstone, Sixth Street And Other Lenders
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 9, 2026
Waymo Secures $5 Billion Debt Financing From PIMCO, Blackstone, Sixth Street And Other Lenders
Waymo closed a $5 billion term loan, marking the autonomous driving company’s first debt financing as it continues expanding its commercial operations in the United States and internationally. PIMCO, Blackstone, and Sixth Street participated as lead syndicated lenders in the financing. Capital Group, Loomis Sayles, and T. Rowe Price also participated as significant lenders.
Additional lenders included Apollo, Blue Owl, Diameter Capital Partners, Franklin Templeton, Fidelity Management & Research Company, HPS Investment Partners, and Oaktree.
Goldman Sachs served as the sole lead bookrunner for the transaction.
The debt financing follows a $16 billion equity investment Waymo closed earlier in 2026 to accelerate the expansion of the Waymo Driver and the company’s autonomous ride-hailing business.
Waymo said the addition of debt capital gives it greater financial flexibility while strengthening its balance sheet as it scales its operations.
The company has been expanding its commercial footprint rapidly and recently launched service in its 15th U.S. city.
Waymo has also announced plans to enter additional international markets as it looks to extend its autonomous driving technology beyond the United States.
The company said proceeds from the term loan will support the continued expansion of its fully autonomous ride-hailing service across domestic and international markets.
Waymo’s ability to raise debt represents another step in its transition from a technology development operation into a larger commercial transportation business.
The company has historically relied heavily on equity capital to finance development of its autonomous driving technology, fleet operations, mapping infrastructure, vehicle integration, and geographic expansion.
Adding a large term loan provides Waymo with another source of capital as it increases fleet deployments and enters additional cities.
Waymo said its growing commercial momentum allowed it to complement its equity financing with debt while preserving flexibility for future growth opportunities.
The financing also brings a broad group of major institutional credit investors onto Waymo’s capital structure, including alternative asset managers, traditional investment managers, and private credit firms.
Waymo said it intends to continue scaling its autonomous ride-hailing network while maintaining its focus on road safety and transportation accessibility.
The company’s Waymo Driver technology operates vehicles without a human driver and is designed to support fully autonomous passenger transportation.
As the company expands, capital requirements could include additional vehicles, fleet facilities, charging and maintenance infrastructure, technology development, and the operational resources required to support new markets.
Waymo described the financing as an important milestone in its development as a scaling commercial enterprise and said the additional capital will help it move faster while expanding thoughtfully.

“Our strong momentum has enabled us to complement our equity financing with debt, providing additional financial flexibility to strengthen our balance sheet and position us to capitalize on the significant opportunities ahead.”

articles.title: U.S. Energy Department Announces Up To $4.2 Billion For Vistra Nuclear Upgrades In Pennsylvania And Ohio
articles.snippet:
The U.S. Department of Energy's Office of Energy Dominance Financing has announced a conditional loan commitment of up to $4.2 billion to finance nuclear uprates and modernization projects across Vistra's nuclear fleet in Pennsylvania and Ohio.
The post U.S. Energy Department Announces Up To $4.2 Billion For Vistra Nuclear Upgrades In Pennsylvania And Ohio appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
U.S. Energy Department Announces Up To $4.2 Billion For Vistra Nuclear Upgrades In Pennsylvania And Ohio
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 7, 2026
U.S. Energy Department Announces Up To $4.2 Billion For Vistra Nuclear Upgrades In Pennsylvania And Ohio
The U.S. Department of Energy’s Office of Energy Dominance Financing has announced a conditional loan commitment of up to $4.2 billion to finance nuclear uprates and modernization projects across Vistra’s nuclear fleet in Pennsylvania and Ohio.
The financing is intended to increase electricity production from existing nuclear facilities, support continued plant operation, and address growing electricity demand across the 13-state PJM Interconnection region.
Vistra’s planned investments encompass the Beaver Valley nuclear facility in Pennsylvania and the Davis-Besse and Perry plants in Ohio.
Together, the projects are expected to preserve nearly 4 GW of existing baseload nuclear generation, which the Energy Department said is enough to power more than 3 million homes.
The projects are also expected to add 433 MW of new nuclear generating capacity through improvements to existing facilities.
Rather than requiring entirely new generating stations or comparable new transmission corridors, the projects are designed to extract additional output from plants that are already operating.
The investments are expected to support approximately 3,000 project-related jobs spanning engineering, construction and planned outage work while helping preserve thousands of permanent jobs associated with the nuclear facilities.
The planned investments are also expected to support operation of the plants for an additional 20 years beyond their existing licenses.
The conditional commitment includes an option for the Energy Department to finance potential future nuclear uprates at Vistra’s Comanche Peak Nuclear Power Plant in Texas.
The financing advances the federal government’s broader strategy of extending existing nuclear generation and increasing electricity production from the U.S. nuclear fleet.
However, the $4.2 billion commitment remains conditional.
Vistra must satisfy technical, legal, environmental and financial requirements before the Energy Department enters into definitive financing agreements and begins funding the loan.
KEY QUOTES:
“President Trump promised to unleash an American nuclear renaissance, and the Energy Department is delivering. By getting more power out of the nuclear plants we already have, we can deliver more affordable, reliable, around-the-clock energy for American families and businesses.”
Chris Wright, U.S. Secretary of Energy
“President Trump and Secretary Wright have set a clear direction for America’s nuclear future, and EDF is financing the projects that advance that mission. These investments will extend the life of existing reactors, increase nuclear generation, and deliver abundant, around-the-clock power to lower costs and power American prosperity for decades to come.”
Gregory A. Beard, Director of the Office of Energy Dominance Financing

articles.title: Ares Raises $4.2 Billion For Inaugural Global Structured Solutions Strategy
articles.snippet:
Ares Management has raised approximately $4.2 billion for its inaugural Ares Global Structured Solutions Fund and affiliated vehicles, significantly exceeding the strategy's original $1 billion fundraising target.
The post Ares Raises $4.2 Billion For Inaugural Global Structured Solutions Strategy appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Ares Raises $4.2 Billion For Inaugural Global Structured Solutions Strategy
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 1, 2026
Ares Raises $4.2 Billion For Inaugural Global Structured Solutions Strategy
Ares Management has raised approximately $4.2 billion for its inaugural Ares Global Structured Solutions Fund and affiliated vehicles, significantly exceeding the strategy’s original $1 billion fundraising target.
The fund, known as AGSS, is managed by the Ares Private Equity Secondaries team and is designed to provide flexible capital solutions to private equity managers pursuing a range of strategic objectives.
Ares plans to use the strategy to partner with managers seeking capital to increase their general partner commitments to funds, seed new strategies through structured limited partner commitments and facilitate succession planning.
The strategy gives Ares a dedicated pool of capital for structured GP solutions as private equity firms seek alternatives to traditional fundraising and financing structures.
Ares said its funds have deployed nearly $9 billion across structured solutions transactions since 2013, giving the firm more than a decade of experience in this part of the secondaries market.
The new fund is intended to increase the scale at which Ares can work with private equity managers while expanding the types of financing and liquidity solutions available through its Secondaries platform.
In addition to structured solutions, Ares’ GP-focused offerings include continuation vehicles and GP stakes, giving the firm multiple ways to provide capital to asset managers and their underlying portfolios.
The fundraising also broadens Ares’ Private Equity Secondaries strategy at a time when private markets managers are increasingly seeking capital for fund commitments, new product launches, ownership transitions and other strategic initiatives.
Ares Private Equity Secondaries is part of the broader Ares Secondaries Group, which has more than 30 years of experience providing liquidity solutions to limited partners and general partners across private equity, real estate, infrastructure and credit.
The Ares Secondaries Group managed approximately $44 billion of assets as of June 30, 2026.
Across its broader platform, Ares Management had more than $671 billion in assets under management as of June 30. The company operates across North America, South America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East and invests across credit, real estate, private equity and infrastructure.
KEY QUOTES:
“The successful close of AGSS highlights the increasing demand for tailored GP solutions in today’s market environment and the innovative leadership of the Ares Secondaries platform. Throughout the firm’s history, Ares has been a close partner to leading managers, and AGSS expands upon our existing GP capabilities, providing creative solutions for their growth initiatives. AGSS reflects the breadth and scale of our platform as well as the confidence of our LPs in this significant market opportunity.”
Blair Jacobson, Co-President of Ares

articles.title: MidOcean Energy Secures More Than $4 Billion In Equity Commitments To Accelerate Global LNG Growth
articles.snippet:
MidOcean Energy has concluded its 2026 equity capital raise with more than $4 billion of closed and pending equity commitments secured over the past 12 months, giving the liquefied natural gas company additional capital to expand its global LNG portfolio.
The post MidOcean Energy Secures More Than $4 Billion In Equity Commitments To Accelerate Global LNG Growth appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
MidOcean Energy Secures More Than $4 Billion In Equity Commitments To Accelerate Global LNG Growth
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 1, 2026
MidOcean Energy Secures More Than $4 Billion In Equity Commitments To Accelerate Global LNG Growth
MidOcean Energy has concluded its 2026 equity capital raise with more than $4 billion of closed and pending equity commitments secured over the past 12 months, giving the liquefied natural gas company additional capital to expand its global LNG portfolio.
The total significantly exceeded MidOcean’s original $2 billion target and includes commitments from new strategic and institutional investors along with significant additional commitments from existing shareholders.
MidOcean Energy was formed and is managed by EIG and is building a diversified global portfolio of LNG assets.
New investors participating in the capital raise include the Private Department of Sheikh Mohammed bin Khalid Al Nahyan, Idemitsu Kosan, NYK Line through Diamond Gas MidOcean, The Arab Energy Fund, Shizuoka Gas and certain Korean institutional investors.
The investor group includes strategic companies, sovereign-linked institutions and financial investors, giving MidOcean a broader capital base as it evaluates additional LNG investments.
MidOcean plans to use the capital to increase balance-sheet flexibility and pursue a pipeline of growth opportunities spanning both operating, cash-generating LNG assets and development-stage projects.
The company has already assembled an LNG portfolio with interests across Canada, Australia, the United States and Latin America. It also has an LNG shipping and marketing presence in Singapore and corporate headquarters in London.
MidOcean said it will continue evaluating additional opportunities consistent with its investment strategy, with an emphasis on building a diversified portfolio that can generate cash flow while providing long-term growth optionality.
The fundraising comes as MidOcean continues to position LNG as a major component of energy security and global economic growth. The company believes geographic diversification can become particularly important during periods of market disruption because a global portfolio provides multiple potential supply and delivery points.
The additional capital gives MidOcean greater capacity to pursue transactions as LNG projects require substantial funding and long development timelines.
MidOcean is backed by EIG, which specializes in energy and energy-related infrastructure investments. EIG had approximately $27.1 billion in assets under management as of June 30, 2026.
During its 44-year history, EIG has committed more than $55 billion to 429 projects or companies across 44 countries and six continents.
KEY QUOTES:
“The progress achieved in this capital raise represents a major milestone for MidOcean and supports our strategy of building a scaled, diversified and resilient global LNG platform. We are pleased to welcome a distinguished group of new investors and thank our existing shareholders for their continued support and confidence.”
“We believe LNG will continue to play an essential role in supporting energy security and global economic growth, and that MidOcean is well positioned to benefit from these long-term market fundamentals. Current events also highlight the importance of geographic diversification with the ability to reliably serve clients from multiple delivery points.”
R. Blair Thomas, Chairman of MidOcean Energy and Chief Executive Officer of EIG

articles.snippet:
Nebius Group has secured a $3.5 billion senior secured financing facility from Citi to support the continued expansion of its global AI infrastructure footprint. The 364-day facility will provide additional capital for data center development, GPU procurement, and general corporate purposes as Nebius continues building out capacity for its AI cloud platform.
The post Nebius Secures $3.5 Billion Citi Facility To Fund AI Data Center And GPU Expansion appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Nebius Secures $3.5 Billion Citi Facility To Fund AI Data Center And GPU Expansion
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 22, 2026
Nebius Secures $3.5 Billion Citi Facility To Fund AI Data Center And GPU Expansion
Nebius Group has secured a $3.5 billion senior secured financing facility from Citi to support the continued expansion of its global AI infrastructure footprint. The 364-day facility will provide additional capital for data center development, GPU procurement, and general corporate purposes as Nebius continues building out capacity for its AI cloud platform.
The financing initially bears interest at Term SOFR plus 2.75% per year, with the spread increasing up to a maximum of 3.50% per year, subject to additional adjustments.
Nebius said the facility is part of a broader strategy to diversify and sequence its sources of capital while maintaining flexibility over when and how it raises longer-term financing.
The company’s funding base also includes customer prepayments, operating cash flows, and other financing mechanisms. By adding the Citi facility, Nebius said it can support near-term expansion while preserving the ability to access other forms of capital for growth in 2027 and beyond.
Nebius is also evaluating asset-backed financing supported by long-term customer commitments. The company said it currently has more than $40 billion of investment-grade customer commitments under long-term contracts, providing another potential source of financing as its infrastructure requirements grow.
Citi served as mandated lead arranger, agent, and security agent for the transaction.
Nebius is building a full-stack AI cloud platform designed for developers and enterprises working across model training, data infrastructure, production deployment, AI agents, and other AI services.
The Amsterdam-based company has been expanding its global data center and compute capacity to meet rising demand for GPU infrastructure. The new facility gives Nebius more financial flexibility as it continues to invest in hardware, capacity, and supporting infrastructure.
Nebius said the financing reflects its approach of maintaining a disciplined balance sheet while matching different funding sources to specific stages of its growth plans.
KEY QUOTES:
“We continue to execute our funding strategy as planned, and are pleased to have secured this financing from a leading global financial institution. This is a result of our disciplined approach to managing our balance sheet to fund our portfolio of projects, and once again demonstrates our ability to choose when and how we raise capital to support our growth.
“Sequencing our financing is how we optimize our long-term cost of capital. This facility provides additional financing to support our near-term capacity build-out. We still have a range of capital sources available to us to finance the next phase of growth, including asset-backed financing based on investment-grade customer commitments of more than $40 billion of long-term contracts.”
Ophir Nave, Chief Operating Officer Of Nebius

articles.title: EnCap Investments Closes $3.5 Billion Minerals Continuation Vehicle For Permian Basin Assets
articles.snippet:
EnCap Investments has closed a continuation vehicle with approximately $3.5 billion in capital commitments for EnCap Minerals and Rock River Minerals, giving the firm and its partners additional time to retain exposure to a large portfolio of Permian Basin mineral and royalty interests.
The post EnCap Investments Closes $3.5 Billion Minerals Continuation Vehicle For Permian Basin Assets appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
EnCap Investments Closes $3.5 Billion Minerals Continuation Vehicle For Permian Basin Assets
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 19, 2026
EnCap Investments Closes $3.5 Billion Minerals Continuation Vehicle For Permian Basin Assets
EnCap Investments has closed a continuation vehicle with approximately $3.5 billion in capital commitments for EnCap Minerals and Rock River Minerals, giving the firm and its partners additional time to retain exposure to a large portfolio of Permian Basin mineral and royalty interests.
The vehicle is managed by EnCap and anchored by funds affiliated with Melange Capital Partners. EnCap said investor demand exceeded the amount required for the transaction, with participation from both existing investors and new institutional investors.
According to EnCap, the transaction represents the largest capital raise to date for a continuation vehicle focused on the upstream energy sector. It also provides existing investors with a liquidity option while allowing EnCap and participating investors to continue owning the assets and receiving exposure to their long-term cash flows.
The underlying portfolio was assembled through partnerships with Fortis Minerals, OGX Resources, Piedra Energy III, and Pegasus Resources. Pegasus continues to manage the assets.
The portfolio consists of approximately 134,000 net royalty acres of mineral and royalty interests in the core of the Permian Basin and currently generates net production of approximately 37,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day.
Activity across the acreage is supported by several major Permian operators. ExxonMobil, Diamondback Energy, Occidental, and ConocoPhillips collectively account for approximately 48% of activity across the portfolio, according to EnCap.
Unlike many operating energy assets, mineral and royalty interests generally do not require the mineral owner to fund drilling and development capital expenditures. EnCap highlighted that characteristic as part of the portfolio’s long-duration cash-flow profile and said the assets provide exposure to high-quality development inventory and operator economics in the Lower 48.
The continuation vehicle expands EnCap’s ability to hold the mineral portfolio beyond the typical life of the funds that initially acquired and developed the assets. The structure also creates a mechanism for investors seeking liquidity to exit while other investors maintain or establish exposure to the assets.
EnCap has been investing in the U.S. energy industry since 1988. The firm has raised 25 institutional investment funds totaling more than $47 billion and currently manages capital for more than 350 U.S. and international investors.
Evercore served as exclusive financial advisor to EnCap on the continuation vehicle, while Kirkland & Ellis served as EnCap’s legal counsel. Latham & Watkins advised Melange on the transaction.
KEY QUOTES:
“We are grateful to our limited partners for their continued support and for the opportunity to keep owning this exceptional asset well into the future. We have long held strong conviction in the Permian Basin, and we believe it will remain a critical economic engine for many years to come, particularly as industry innovation continues.”

articles.title: Sarvam AI in Talks to Raise $300 Mn at $3 Bn Valuation: Report
articles.snippet: Sarvam AI in Talks to Raise $300 Mn at $3 Bn Valuation: Report Analytics India Magazine
articles.text:
Listen 5 min
SHARE Save
Follow Preferred Source Google News WhatsApp Telegram
Bengaluru-based AI startup Sarvam AI is in early discussions to raise $250 million to $300 million at a valuation of $3 billion, potentially doubling its valuation in four months, according to an ET report.
The proposed funding round could make Sarvam the most highly valued AI startup in India. The amount being raised and the valuation could change as discussions progress, the report added.
Sarvam AI is also reportedly in talks with large domestic enterprises and institutions as it seeks to keep a substantial shareholding with Indian entities. The discussions are at an early stage.
AIM reached out to Sarvam AI for confirmation. The company had not responded at the time of publication.
In June, Sarvam raised $234 million in the first close of its $300 million Series B round at a post-money valuation of $1.5 billion. HCLTech led the round with a $150 million investment, alongside Bessemer Venture Partners and existing investors Khosla Ventures and Peak XV Partners. NVIDIA and IndiGo Ventures participated in a $75 million extension .
Founded by Vivek Raghavan and Pratyush Kumar in 2023, Sarvam develops Indian-language AI models and applications for government agencies and businesses, with a focus on sectors such as banking and insurance. Its customers include Life Insurance Corporation of India, SBI Life, IDFC First Bank, Tata Capital and CRED.
The company is expanding its efforts across AI models, computing infrastructure and enterprise deployments. It plans to build a trillion-parameter AI model and establish an office in San Francisco to recruit researchers. Sarvam has also hired Sashikumar Sreedharan, the former head of Google Cloud India.
Sarvam’s Indus AI workspace has received approval for deployment across Maharashtra government departments for tasks such as drafting, translation and document analysis. Government data for the deployment will be hosted within India.
